_comment: Observed worst-case durations of long-running ci.yml jobs on MAIN, and the
input to check_job_timeout_headroom.py. Refresh with:
npm run check:ci-timeout-headroom -- --refresh
which reads the GitHub Actions API. The GATE itself never touches the
network: it compares these committed numbers against the timeout-minutes
in the workflow, so `npm run ci` stays offline-safe.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. On 2026-08-07 `Validate Promotion` hit its
timeout-minutes: 30 at 30m13s. A timed-out job's conclusion is `cancelled`,
and assert-ci-complete.sh forgives `skipped` but NOT `cancelled`, so CI
Complete and Pipeline Sentinel failed and the finalize step never dispatched
cd-v2.yml. The 0804-1 release did not ship, and no error message anywhere
said the word `timeout` -- the job log's only clue is `The operation was
canceled.` It had ALSO timed out on 2026-07-28 and nobody noticed, because
the ceiling was approached silently for weeks: 21m57s, 27m20s, CANCELLED
31m03s, 28m35s, 24m09s, 24m56s, 24m01s, CANCELLED 30m51s.
A PR cannot catch this class. PR runs promote the tiny per-PR channel and
finish in ~7m; main promotes the full `edge` channel, which grows with every
release. So the check is not `did it pass` but `how much headroom is left`.
REFRESHED FROM ONE RUN ON PURPOSE, 2026-08-21. The default --runs 8 window
straddles an implementation change and is therefore WRONG here: it recorded
3421s (57m01s) for Validate Promotion, a worst case belonging to the
download-and-reupload copy that console#570 DELETED. 3421s x 1.50 demands an
86-minute ceiling, i.e. exactly the raise the validate-promote comment in
ci.yml forbids, so honouring that number would have undone the fix.
The post-fix copy is server-side (aws s3api copy-object) and ran the FULL
edge channel in 1026s (17m06s) on run 32491717875, against 61m12s cancelled
on 2026-08-20 and 57m01s on 2026-08-18. Only that one run exists on the new
implementation, so samples=1 is the honest maximum rather than a shortcut.
THE WEAKNESS, stated rather than hidden: one sample means one unusually fast
run could set the bar. Re-refresh with the default window once several main
runs have accumulated on the server-side copy; the number should stay near
1000s and the margin near 3.5x. If a later refresh ever pushes the margin
under 1.50x again, the fix is NOT to raise timeout-minutes, which has already
been raised once from 30 to 60. Suspect the apt/dnf/apk/pacman install steps
that run after the copy, since the copy itself is no longer O(channel size).
